author: Ahmed Ibrahim
title: Bonnaroo 2025: Totem Keeps Festival Spirit Alive
text:
Bonnaroo Faces Crossroads After Third Cancellation in Five Years The future of the iconic Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival is in question following a rain-soaked cancellation, raising concerns about infrastructure and preparedness as organizers vow to address fan frustrations.
Bonnaroo weekend has long been a highly anticipated experience in the festival circuit, celebrated for its unique atmosphere and devoted community. However, with its third cancellation in five years, the festival faces a critical juncture, prompting questions about its long-term viability. Anyone who’s attended Bonnaroo will speak to its absolute uniqueness; the vibe is something unmatched and unreplicable.
The festival, which typically hosts around 80,000 attendees, prides itself on a mantra of “Radiate positivity,” a lack of overt sponsorship on stages, a diverse range of acts, and sets that extend into the early morning hours. This year’s event promised a refreshed experience, with plans for improvements to the grounds and the introduction of the Infinity Stage – a 360-degree sound system touted as the first of its size in the United States, replacing the Who Stage. The Totem Compass team also planned to enhance the festival experience with an interactive map and meet-ups through their friend-finding app, designed to function even without cell service.
However, those plans were abruptly halted by torrential rains and lightning storms that began on Friday afternoon. Festival-goers sought shelter in their cars, awaiting a cancellation that ultimately came, leaving many with unlivable camping conditions. Despite the challenging circumstances, the spirit of Bonnaroo persevered, with attendees organizing slip-and-slides, mud wrestling matches, puppet shows, and even an impromptu set from John Summit in the artist RV park.
The fallout from the cancellation was swift and critical. Lines to exit the festival stretched for over four hours, and frustrations mounted over what many perceived as a lack of preparation for the forecasted storms. Reports surfaced of abandoned medic tents, locked showers, and a significant lack of communication from festival organizers in the immediate aftermath. A majority of the volunteers, compensated only with festival wristbands, reportedly walked out, leaving attendees to fend for themselves. “There was a stark lack of communication in the first few hours after the cancellation was announced,” one attendee noted.
Amidst the chaos, the SPIN team relied on the Totem Compass technology to reconnect after being separated while navigating the grounds. They found the app’s map particularly useful for locating remaining vendors and finding their way back to camp. Artists scheduled to perform, including John Summit, HAYLA, Flipturn, Die Spitz, Courting, Wilderado, and Hey Nothing, had also been gifted Totem Compasses to stay connected with their crews. HAYLA remarked that she often gets lost at festivals, a problem the technology aimed to solve. Flipturn joked that their drummer, known for wandering, would now be easily located.
While the weather ultimately derailed the event, Bonnaroo initially offered a 75% refund, a decision that drew further criticism. Following feedback from attendees, the festival updated its policy to offer full refunds and pledged to address concerns about the grounds. Organizers have promised to “do right by their fans” and invest in improvements to the farm and event organization.
In the wake of the cancellation, fans and artists alike organized pop-up shows in Nashville and Chattanooga, demonstrating the enduring sense of community surrounding the festival. Attendees greeted each other with a bittersweet “Happy Roo,” embodying the festival’s ethos of positivity even in disappointment.
The road to recovery for Bonnaroo will require significant investment and a commitment to addressing the concerns raised by attendees. Suggestions range from upgrading the campgrounds with improved drainage and wood chips to relocating the festival to the fall to avoid increasingly volatile spring weather. While the future remains uncertain, the spirit of Bonnaroo – and the desire to “Radiate Positivity” – lives on.
